answer: Sybil resistance follows because every identity must complete a continuously verified chain of sequential modular squarings, where each result depends on the preceding one. An attacker can create clones, but cannot parallelize one chain across GPUs to reduce its physical latency; additional hardware only repeats the cost. Wesolowski proofs make verification fast, so an ocean of forged identities remains time-bound by the quartz-clocked protocol window, while an island of honest nodes can validate them efficiently.
